Its single retry was meant to absorb transient timeouts, but the wrapper's own abort-timeout message 'ETIMEDOUT after 60000ms (TICKER/fts)' does not contain lowercase 'timeout', so the retry never fires for the most common timeout — the FTS fetch is marked ftsFetchFailed and the whole ticker is thrown/failed on the first timeout. This directly worsens coverage under Yahoo throttling and wastes the partial work already done.
nonScoring.fix: Reuse the same robust timeout/network predicate as quoteSummaryWithRetry (extract it into a shared `isRetryable(e)` helper checking name, constructor.name, and a case-INSENSITIVE regex including ETIMEDOUT/ESOCKETTIMEDOUT/EAI_AGAIN/ECONNRESET). Failure mode prevented: expensive FTS calls failing the whole ticker on a retryable wrapper-timeout because the literal substring check missed 'ETIMEDOUT'.

nonScoring.title: FX `scale()` applies the reporting `factor` to balance-sheet/annual rows including share-count-like or unit-less fields that slip past the annualShares guard (e.g. annualBalance has no share field, but timeseries/annual maps blindly multiply every numeric key)
nonScoring.evidence: Line 384-387 (`scale`) multiplies EVERY numeric property of a balance-sheet-style object by `factor`. annual loop (446-455) skips only the literal key 'annualShares'; timeseries loop (457-461) skips nothing. Any currency-amount field is correctly scaled, but the design relies on a hardcoded single-key skip-list ('annualShares') and on the assumption that every other numeric field in annual/timeseries/balance rows is currency-denominated. mapFTSToBalance now adds fields like (none unit-less today) — but the pattern is a landmine: the comment at 416-430 even acknowledges a metrics.* allow-list was needed for exactly this reason, yet annual/timeseries/balance use a blind deny-nothing multiply.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: The metrics.* path was hardened to an explicit allow-list (CCY_DENOMINATED_METRICS, 423) precisely because blind scaling silently corrupts non-currency fields. The annual/timeseries/balance paths still scale-everything with only a one-off 'annualShares' exception. Any future balance field that is a ratio, count, or per-share number (e.g. a sharesIssued, employeeCount, or a days-ratio) added to mapFTSToBalance/_arr will be silently FX-multiplied — the same bug class that NEW-4 fixed for annualShares, waiting to recur. Structurally caps trust in the FX layer.
nonScoring.fix: Invert annual/timeseries/balance scaling to an explicit allow-list of currency-denominated keys (mirroring CCY_DENOMINATED_METRICS), or tag each annual field with a unit at construction and scale only `unit==='ccy'` fields. Comment naming the failure mode: 'blind per-key FX multiply silently scales any future non-currency field'.

nonScoring.title: Absence-as-zero debt summing `(std || 0) + (ltd || 0)` treats a legitimately reported 0 identically to a missing line, and the `|| 0` falsy fallback also collapses a real 0 debt into the 'present' branch — the _debtPartial flag can mislabel a genuine zero-debt company
nonScoring.evidence: Line 696: `const totalDebt = (std == null && ltd == null) ? null : (std || 0) + (ltd || 0);` and 697 `_debtPartial = totalDebt != null && (std == null || ltd == null)`. The null-vs-present decision uses `== null` (correct), but the SUM uses `std || 0` / `ltd || 0` — a real reported debt of exactly 0 is indistinguishable from null in the addition (both contribute 0, which is fine arithmetically) BUT a company that reports std=0 (true zero current debt) and ltd=null is flagged `_debtPartial` with reason 'no-long-term-debt', conflating 'Yahoo omitted the line' with 'company has long-term debt we couldn't read'. The brief explicitly calls out '|| 0 falsy bugs (0 legitimately valid)'.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: 12.4% of snapshots carry _debtPartial (per the in-file note at 683). The reason string (no-current-debt vs no-long-term-debt) is consumed by downstream leverage methods to size understatement. Because `== null` is used for the partial decision this is mostly correct, but the residual issue is that a TRUE zero in one leg with a missing other leg is reported as partial-understated when it may be complete — over-flagging leverage uncertainty on genuinely low-debt names. The asymmetry between the `== null` partial-check and the `|| 0` sum is the smell.
nonScoring.fix: Keep the deliberate absence-as-zero sum (changing it is out of scope per constraints), but distinguish reported-zero from missing in the _debtPartial reason: flag partial only when the missing leg is `== null` AND the present leg is > 0 (i.e. there is actual debt that the missing leg could materially add to). Comment naming the failure mode: 'reported-zero debt leg mis-flagged as partial/understated'.

nonScoring.title: annualShares fallback chain can mix share-count bases across years: primary tries dilutedAverageShares per-year, and ONLY if the ENTIRE array is all-null falls back to basicAverageShares/ordinarySharesNumber — so a partially-populated diluted series is never backfilled from basic, leaving year-gaps
nonScoring.evidence: Lines 1863-1868: `ftsAnnualShares = _ftsExtractByYear(fts.annualFin, ['dilutedAverageShares','basicAverageShares']); if (!ftsAnnualShares.some(v => v != null)) { ftsAnnualShares = _ftsExtractByYear(fts.annualBs, ['ordinarySharesNumber','shareIssued']); }`. The `.some(v => v != null)` test only triggers the balance-sheet fallback when EVERY year is null. A series with diluted shares for years 0-2 but null for year 3 keeps the null — no per-year backfill — and the balance-sheet path is skipped entirely.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: buyback-yield.js and capital-allocation-quality.js zip annualShares across years to compute share-count change. A mid-window null produces a gap that those methods treat as incomputable for that span, OR (worse) if they index-align, pairs a diluted-basis count against a basic-basis count from a sibling array. Partial coverage is the common case for international/FTS-sparse names, so this under-populates exactly the universe the screener is trying to expand into. It also silently mixes diluted vs basic share bases within one array via the `_ftsValue` multi-key fallback (a row with no diluted but a basic field yields basic for that year — a basis mismatch across years of the SAME array).
nonScoring.fix: Build annualShares per-year with an explicit basis preference and record which basis each year used (diluted > basic > ordinary), backfilling per-year rather than all-or-nothing, and store a parallel basis tag so consumers can reject mixed-basis spans. Failure mode prevented: mixed diluted/basic share bases and unfilled year-gaps corrupting buyback/dilution math.

nonScoring.title: gradeSnapshot runs on the canonical AFTER FX conversion and mcap filter but its result is preserved verbatim across price-only refreshes while nanRatio/missingFields are nulled — a snapshot can carry a stale grade computed from a different field set than it now contains
nonScoring.evidence: Full pull computes `canonical._quality = gradeSnapshot(canonical)` (2107). Price-only path (1650-1655) preserves `existing._quality.grade` but nulls nanRatio and missingFields, with a long justification (Tag 232c-12) that price-only doesn't change field presence. That is true for price-only, BUT the schema-stale (Tag 211l) and currency-stale probes can flip a snapshot's field set on a full pull while an OLDER snapshot kept its grade through many price-only cycles before the full pull triggered.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: score-aggregator's DATAQUALITY_ENFORCE tier-cap reads _quality.grade. The grade is a categorical bucket that is mostly robust, and the team deliberately preserves it — so this is low severity. The residual risk: a grade computed before Tag 211l fields existed is carried forward as (say) 'B' even though the current snapshot now lacks fields a fresh grade would penalize. Mostly self-correcting on the next full pull. Flagged for completeness as a data-provenance subtlety, not a live corruption.
nonScoring.fix: Stamp _quality with the schema/tag version it was computed under (e.g. _quality.gradedSchema = FTS_CACHE_VERSION or a snapshot-schema tag) so score-aggregator can distinguish a current grade from one preserved across refreshes, and force a re-grade when the schema tag advances. No change to the preserve-on-price-only behavior itself.

nonScoring.title: Market-cap thresholds and the Cap≥ filter compare raw local-currency marketCap against USD constants — no FX normalization
nonScoring.evidence: Line 281: `const mcap = unwrap(stock.marketCap) || 0;` (taken verbatim, no currency conversion). SMALL classification line 715: `if (r.mcap > 0 && r.mcap < 2e9 && ...)`. Client filter line 1650: `if (r.mcap == null || r.mcap < (+filterMinMcap) * 1e9) return false;` and the UI label line 4237: `title="Market cap minimum in billions USD"`. REGION_TO_COUNTRY (lines 45-58) shows the universe spans Tokyo/XETRA/HKSE/KSE/Paris/etc. — i.e. JPY/EUR/HKD/KRW-denominated caps.

A Tokyo name with ¥150B (~$1B) has mcap=150e9, so `r.mcap < 2e9` is false and it is silently dropped from the SMALL tab even though it IS a sub-$2B company; conversely the `Cap≥ $B` filter treats a ¥-cap as if it were USD, so the user's '≥$1B' filter admits/excludes the wrong stocks across every non-USD market. This is asymmetric survivorship attrition concentrated in foreign exchanges and a direct cause of the 'SMALL cap hunting' tab missing real candidates.
nonScoring.fix: Normalize marketCap to USD at build time using the snapshot's reported currency (Yahoo exposes `financialCurrency`/`currency`) times a daily FX rate, store mcapUsd on the row, and use mcapUsd for the $2B SMALL gate and the Cap≥ filter. If a stock's currency or FX rate is unavailable, flag it (e.g. mcapCurrencyUnknown) rather than comparing a raw figure against USD constants. Do NOT hardcode ticker exclusions.

nonScoring.title: g-chord keyboard shortcuts navigate to tabs whose buttons were removed (Tag 243), producing an orphan view
nonScoring.evidence: Line 3712: `const map = { h:'HG', q:'QC', b:'BF', s:'SMALL', r:'R40', p:'PRE_BREAKOUT', w:'WATCH' };` then `switchToTab(tab)`. switchToTab's only guard (line 3462) is `if (!TABS[tabKey] && tabKey !== 'SECTOR') return;` — TABS['HG'/'QC'/'BF'/'PRE_BREAKOUT'/'WATCH'] still exist (data is still classified and embedded), so the guard passes and activeTab becomes a tab with NO visible button. nonScoring.title: unwrap() only reads `.value`; a Yahoo {raw,fmt} envelope or a {value:'12.3'} string silently becomes null
nonScoring.evidence: Lines 73-78: `function unwrap(v){ if (v==null) return null; if (typeof v==='number') return Number.isFinite(v)?v:null; if (typeof v==='object' && Number.isFinite(v.value)) return v.value; return null; }`. Every headline metric is funneled through it (lines 281, 285-289: marketCap, revenueGrowthYoY, grossMargin, operatingMargin, fcfMarginTTM, revenueTTM). A raw Yahoo field of shape `{raw: 12.3, fmt: '12.3'}` (no `.value`) returns null; a stringified `{value:'12.3'}` also returns null because Number.isFinite('12.3') is false.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: If any upstream snapshot field is ever stored as a Yahoo {raw,fmt} envelope or a numeric string (a single change in the pull/normalization layer, or one feed field that escaped normalization), the metric silently disappears as null instead of failing loudly — the row keeps building, lands in tabs with '—' cells, and quietly drops out of R40/growth/mcap gates. Silent null-coercion of the core metrics is exactly the kind of asymmetric attrition the audit targets.
nonScoring.fix: Harden unwrap to also accept the envelope and coerce strings: check `Number.isFinite(v.raw)` then `Number.isFinite(v.value)`, and `const n=Number(v); return Number.isFinite(n)?n:null` for string inputs. Optionally count and log unwrap-misses per field so a normalization regression is visible rather than silent.

nonScoring.title: Modal Score-History sparkline and R40-tab Trend always plot hgScore even on QC/R40/BF context, mislabeled 'HG Score'
nonScoring.evidence: Modal Section D (lines 2643-2644) builds the sparkline only from hgScore: `const hgSeries = sh.history.slice().reverse().map(e => (e && Number.isFinite(e.hgScore)) ? e.hgScore : null);` titled 'HG Score (last Nd)'. trendCell (lines 1892-1896) for R40/KI_INFRA/R40_DURABLE uses `series = ts.r40;` but the comment at 1875-1878 admits 'r40 isn't stored in score-history so the R40 tab falls back to hgScore as a correlated proxy' — and buildProxies (line 4066) only populates trendSpark.r40 when history entries carry an `r40` field, which the snapshot-score-history may not write, leaving R40 trend silently empty or proxied.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: A user reading a QC or R40 candidate's modal sees a sparkline labeled 'HG Score' that is the Hypergrowth axis, not the axis they are screening on — a quietly misleading momentum signal. Low severity (cosmetic/interpretation) but it undermines trust in the Trend column the dashboard heavily advertises.
nonScoring.fix: Pick the history series matching the modal's active context (qcScore for QC, hgScore for HG, bfScore/fallback for BF) and label it accordingly; for the R40 trend, store r40 in score-history (or relabel the column 'HG proxy' so the proxy is explicit).

nonScoring.title: Score-based sorts/`score` column use `Math.max(hgScore||0, qcScore||0, bfScore||0)`, so a genuine 0 ties with missing-score and negative scores are clamped to 0
nonScoring.evidence: Line 1717: `if (k === 'score') return Math.max(b.hgScore||0, b.qcScore||0, b.bfScore||0) - Math.max(a.hgScore||0, ...)`. Same idiom in the WATCH auto sort (1714), WATCH row score (2036), and classifyTabs WATCH sort (821). The `||0` converts null/undefined scores to 0 and any legitimately-zero score is indistinguishable from 'no score'.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: Rows with no computable score for a mode sort as if they scored exactly 0, interleaving with real zero-scorers; a stock scoring 0 in one mode but, say, 35 in another is handled by Math.max so that case is fine, but the `||0` still means 'incomputable' and 'scored zero' are merged in the sort key and in the WATCH score cell. Minor ranking imprecision (0 is a valid screener score, the audit flags the `||0` falsy class explicitly).
nonScoring.fix: Use a null-aware max that returns -Infinity when all three are null/non-finite (so missing-score rows sort last) and only counts finite scores, instead of coercing null to 0.

nonScoring.title: buildRow allocates a fresh Date()/toISOString() per stock and re-derives todayIso inside the per-row loop
nonScoring.evidence: Line 453: `const todayIso = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);` sits inside buildRow, which main() calls once per loaded snapshot (loop at lines 4322-4332 over ~3.5k+ stocks). The value is run-constant.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: Thousands of redundant Date allocations/ISO formats per generator run. Negligible against the 14.6h pull but free to fix and it removes a per-row dependency on wall-clock that could, in theory, straddle UTC midnight mid-run and stamp two different 'today' values across rows.
nonScoring.fix: Compute todayIso once in main() (or at module scope for the run) and pass it into buildRow, mirroring how generatedAt is already computed once in main() at line 4386.

nonScoring.title: growthSource/accelSource/durSource recorded in Schritt 1 but IGNORED in Schritt 2 — cross-sectional z mixes annual & quarterly growth definitions, the exact bug the screen claims to prevent
nonScoring.evidence: court-screen.js:108-110 records `growthSource = gAnnual != null ? 'annual' : (gQ != null ? 'quarterly' : null)` with the comment 'so Schritt 2 can compute anchors per-source ... instead of z-scoring an annual/quarterly-mixed universe'. But court-score.js:207 pools ALL members into one anchor: `const vals = members.map(m => rawOf(m, ax.key)).filter(...); stats[ax.key] = { median: median(vals), mad: mad(vals) ... }` — rawOf(m,'growth') returns m._growth regardless of m.growthSource. Same for accel (accelSource) and the durability axis (durSource). The (raw−median)/MAD z at line 233 therefore compares an annual-YoY grower against a quarterly-YoY grower on one ruler.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: Annual and trailing-4Q YoY growth have different magnitudes and dispersion; pooling them puts every young/quarterly-sourced name on a median/MAD computed mostly from annual reporters (or vice-versa), systematically mis-ranking exactly the young hypergrowth names the screener exists to surface. The comment asserts the bug is fixed; it is not — Schritt 2 never reads the *Source fields. This is a top driver of the screener sitting at ~20% of potential.
nonScoring.fix: In court-score.js, bucket the anchor computation by source: compute separate {median,mad} for members with growthSource==='annual' vs 'quarterly' (and accelSource, durSource) and z-score each member against its own-source anchor. Carry growthSource/accelSource into the candidate record consumption (it is already emitted at court-screen.js:197/202). Comment each branch with the failure mode: '// prevents annual-vs-quarterly z mixing (mis-ranks young quarterly-sourced names)'.

nonScoring.title: Inorganic-growth / M&A detection is cosmetic: pAuth is hardcoded 0, so the flag never affects score — it only prints a lamp
nonScoring.evidence: Line 238-241: `const pAuth = 0; // keine M&A-Daten lokal` then `m.score = Math.max(0, 100 * core - pDil - pAuth)`. The entire data-driven inorganicFlag() machinery (lines 157-165) and the maRpoByTicker snapshot only feed lamps (line 253-254) and a degradedRankBias *string* (line 269). A name flagged 'inorganic' (GEN: M&A-flow-heavy, flat book) receives the identical score it would get unflagged.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: The headline justification for replacing the hardcoded INORGANIC set (lines 110-114) with a 'structural, data-driven' rule is undermined: the rule changes no ranking. GEN's M&A-inflated A1 growth still ranks it as if organic. The whole inorganic apparatus is dead-weight on the score path while reading as a working control.
nonScoring.fix: Wire a bounded, capped penalty (or an A1 haircut) off inorganicFlag(): e.g. when 'inorganic', scale the growth axis contribution down or apply a capped pAuth derived from paymentsToRev/deltaGoodwillPctRev. Keep it capped and continuous (no ticker hardcoding). Comment: '// prevents M&A-bought growth from ranking as organic (GEN flat-book anchor-inversion)'.

nonScoring.title: ma-rpo-snapshot.json read is unguarded — missing/corrupt file throws a raw ENOENT, inconsistent with the named-error guard added 20 lines above for court-buckets.json
nonScoring.evidence: Line 151: `const maRpoByTicker = new Map(readJson(path.join(ROOT, 'data', 'ma-rpo-snapshot.json')).map(r => [r.ticker, r]));` — no try/catch and no env override, while lines 138-146 wrap court-buckets.json in a try/catch that converts ENOENT into an operator-facing message, and CAND/BUCK/OUT all have env overrides (lines 21-23). readJson also does `.replace(/^﻿/, '')` only for a BOM at string start.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: The SaaS A2 forward-book axis (the headline v1.1 feature) silently depends on this file. If it is absent in a test/verify harness or a fresh checkout, the run dies with an opaque ENOENT pointing at no workflow — the opposite of the hardening applied to its sibling artifact. A corrupt/empty file additionally yields an empty Map → every A2 read returns neutral 0 (silent degradation, not a loud failure).
nonScoring.fix: Wrap in the same try/catch+named-error pattern as BUCK (point operator at the M&A/RPO snapshot producer), add a COURT_MARPO env override for isolated harness runs, and assert the parsed array is non-empty before trusting A2 to be 'live' (else mark the bucket degraded).

nonScoring.title: Collapse-reweight recomputes the score from DISPLAY-rounded axis values (axisS, 2 decimals) instead of the full-precision s — lossy, and silently re-derives A2 from a rounded value
nonScoring.evidence: Original scoring uses full precision: line 233 computes `s`, line 235 `core += ax.w * (s + 1) / 2`, and only line 234 stores the rounded copy `m.axisS[ax.name] = Math.round(s * 100) / 100`. But the reweight path at line 296-297 rebuilds core from the rounded copy: `core += w * ((m.axisS[a.name] || 0) + 1) / 2`. So when the durability backstop fires (rhoDomAxis>0.90), every member's score is recomputed at 2-decimal axis precision, including the A2 composite (m._a2) which is only preserved rounded in axisS.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: The haircut path produces a score on a different numerical basis than the normal path; at the margins this reorders near-ties precisely in the regime (durability dominance) where rank stability was the whole point of the Re-Court tie-averaged-Spearman work. `|| 0` also coerces a legitimately-zero-but-present axis identically to a missing one.
nonScoring.fix: Store the unrounded per-axis s on the member (e.g. m._axisRaw[name]) during the first pass and reweight from that; round only for display. Comment: '// reweight from full-precision s, not display-rounded axisS (prevents near-tie reordering under the durability haircut)'.

nonScoring.title: No FX/currency normalization anywhere — revenue, GP, FCF, RPO are taken raw from Yahoo, so scale gates, scaleRevM, mega-cap flag, rpoToRev and cross-sectional medians mix USD and non-USD reporters
nonScoring.evidence: court-screen.js:100 `revLatest = revA[0]`, :127 `scaleRevM = revLatest / 1e6`, with no currency field read from payload. court-score.js:222 gates membership on `log10(Math.max(m.scaleRevM, 1))` against scaleLog.c=log10(50)/2.0; :116 MEGACAP_REVM=15000 ($15B) compared to scaleRevM; A2 rpoToRev (court-score.js:213) and rpoLatest credibility (cred(), :121, floor $50M/$300M) are all USD-assumed. Yahoo reports financials in the issuer's native currency (e.g. ILA, EUR, JPY, KRW).
nonScoring.why_it_matters: A KRW or JPY reporter has revenue numbers 100–1000x a USD peer's, so it sails over the $50M floor and trips MEGACAP/credibility ceilings purely from currency, while an issuer in a weak currency can be wrongly cut. The cross-sectional median/MAD per bucket is computed over a currency-mixed universe, contaminating every z-score. The membership pre-filter even has a comment about asset-light/scale anchors but no FX guard. This is a classic survivorship/normalization data-integrity hole that caps cross-sectional validity.
nonScoring.fix: Read the financialCurrency from the Yahoo payload and convert revenue/GP/FCF/RPO/scale to a single reporting currency (USD) via an as-of FX table before any gate or anchor. If currency is missing, flag the name (lamp) rather than silently treating it as USD. Comment the conversion site with the failure mode it prevents (currency-driven scale/mega-cap misclassification).

nonScoring.title: MAD==0 silently collapses an axis to neutral for the whole bucket — when >50% of members share a value (common after winsorize/rounding), every member's z on that axis becomes 0
nonScoring.evidence: sAxis line 33: `if (raw == null || med == null || m == null || m === 0) return 0; // neutral` — m is the MAD. mad() (line 26) returns 0 whenever the median absolute deviation is 0, i.e. a majority of values are identical. growth/accel are winsorized (court-screen.js via clip) and all values are round()-ed to 4 decimals, increasing tie frequency. When MAD=0 the axis contributes a flat w*(0+1)/2 to every member — it stops discriminating entirely, with no lamp.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: An axis can go fully inert for a bucket (e.g. a small bucket where opMargin or roicMinusWacc clusters) and no diagnostic is emitted — the score looks normal but is effectively (n-1)-dimensional. Quietly caps discrimination and is invisible to the operator, unlike the many other conditions that raise lamps.
nonScoring.fix: When stats[ax.key].mad===0 (or n below a floor), emit a per-bucket 'axis-inert(<name>)' lamp/diagnostic and consider falling back to a scaled-IQR or a tiny epsilon so ties still order by sign. Comment: '// MAD=0 means the axis is non-discriminating for this bucket — surface it instead of silently neutralizing'.

nonScoring.title: No isFinite guard on membership M or final score — a NaN from any axis (e.g. malformed maRpo record feeding _a2, or scaleRevM<=0) propagates to score and corrupts the sort
nonScoring.evidence: Line 223 `const M = mg * mGM * mSc;` and line 241 `m.score = Math.max(0, 100 * core - pDil - pAuth)`. Math.max(0, NaN) === NaN. core accumulates `ax.w * (s + 1) / 2` where s for a2Forward is `m._a2` (line 232), computed by computeA2Forward from snapshot fields with no final isFinite clamp (lines 123-130 can produce NaN if cred() gets a non-numeric base or sAxis gets a non-finite raw that slips the null check). members.sort((a,b)=>b.score-a.score) at line 307 with any NaN score yields an undefined ordering.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: A single bad snapshot row can silently scramble the entire bucket ranking (NaN comparisons make Array.sort order implementation-defined), and a NaN membership mis-buckets In/Borderline/Out. The codebase guards null carefully elsewhere but never guards the non-finite result of the arithmetic.
nonScoring.fix: Clamp at the boundaries: `if (!isFinite(M)) M = 0;` before membershipClass; `m.score = isFinite(m.score) ? m.score : 0;` after line 241 (and after the reweight at line 299), and isFinite-guard computeA2Forward's return. Comment: '// NaN score from a malformed snapshot row must not scramble the sort'.

nonScoring.title: degradedNote is referenced twice but never defined on any FORMULA — always undefined/null; the degraded-mode console banner would print 'undefined'
nonScoring.evidence: Line 309 `degradedNote: F.degradedNote || null` and line 326 `if (R.degraded) console.log(´⚠ DEGRADIERT: ${R.degradedNote}´)`. Grep across court-score.js shows FORMULAS objects define `label`, `degraded`, `a2Note` — there is no `degradedNote` key anywhere. Both formulas currently have degraded:false so line 326 never fires, masking it.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: Latent: the moment any bucket is set degraded:true (the SaaS bucket ran degraded in v1.0 per the header), the operator banner prints 'DEGRADIERT: undefined' instead of the reason — a regression waiting on a config flip. It also signals the degraded-note plumbing was never finished.
nonScoring.fix: Either add a real degradedNote string to any formula that can be degraded, or remove the field and derive the banner text from the actual degrade cause (e.g. the 'A2-missing-degraded' lamp). Keep one source of truth.

nonScoring.title: Dedupe fingerprint can still drop a distinct issuer: round()-ed growth/fcfMargin (4 dp) plus integer scaleRevM means two different companies sharing those 4 values collide, and the kept record is chosen by Map iteration order (non-deterministic w.r.t. which issuer survives)
nonScoring.evidence: Line 189 `const fp = ´${c.gm}|${c.scaleRevM}|${c.growth}|${c.fcfMargin}´`. All four are round()-ed in court-screen.js (gm/growth/fcfMargin to 4 dp at :209, scaleRevM to integer $M at :200). The comment at :187-188 acknowledges the prior (gm,revM) collision but the widened key is still a rounded-value tuple. The survivor is whichever ticker bucketOf yields first (line 178 iterates the bucketOf Map); the loser is only recorded as a _dupDropped lamp on the survivor.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: Two genuinely distinct small caps with coincidentally equal 4dp gm/growth/fcf and equal $M revenue (plausible for rounded small numbers) silently lose one member, and *which* one is kept depends on classification-map ordering rather than any quality criterion. It is better than before but still a silent attrition path with order-dependent outcome.
nonScoring.fix: Key the dedupe on a stable identity (exchange/ISIN/CIK if available in the snapshot) rather than rounded financial values; if only financials are available, compare on unrounded values and require an explicit same-issuer signal. When a collision is genuinely ambiguous, keep both and lamp them rather than dropping. Make survivor selection deterministic (e.g. lexicographic ticker).

nonScoring.title: ROIC proxy hardcodes a 0.79 tax-shield and Schritt 2 applies a single flat WACC=0.09 to every name — the A4 ROIC-WACC axis is effectively a ROIC rank with a constant offset, not a spread
nonScoring.evidence: court-screen.js:181 `roicProxy = (opA[0] * 0.79) / ic` (0.79 = assumed 21% tax, no per-name tax data). court-score.js:106 `const WACC = 0.09; // [TODO-CAL] grober Proxy für A4` and :192 `m.roicMinusWacc = c.roicProxy - WACC`. Subtracting the same constant from every name's ROIC before cross-sectional z (median/MAD) cancels out — the median shifts by exactly 0.09 too — so roicMinusWacc ranks identically to roicProxy alone.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: The A4 'ROIC minus WACC' axis advertises an economic-spread read but, being a constant subtraction ahead of a median-centered z, contributes nothing beyond raw ROIC ordering. Effort/weight (w=0.078) is spent on a relabeled ROIC. Caps the analytic value of the SaaS formula's quality block.
nonScoring.fix: Either drop the WACC subtraction (it is a no-op pre-z) and label the axis honestly as ROIC, or make WACC name-specific (size/beta/leverage proxy) so the spread actually varies cross-sectionally. Tag [TODO-CAL] resolution with the failure mode: 'constant WACC pre-z is a no-op; A4 must vary by name to add signal'.

nonScoring.title: Cache file filter uses a fragile regex to mean 'no exchange suffix' — any US ticker containing a dot (BRK.B, BF.B) is excluded, and the double-extension intent is opaque
nonScoring.evidence: Line 68: `const files = fs.readdirSync(CACHE).filter(f => f.endsWith('.json') && !/\./.test(f.replace(/\.json$/, '')));` — strips the trailing .json then rejects the name if any '.' remains. Intent is to keep no-suffix US names (drop FOO.L, FOO.TO). But class-share US tickers legitimately contain a dot (BRK.B, BF.B, HEI.A), so their cache files are silently skipped.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: Asymmetric survivorship at ingestion: a whole class of legitimate US issuers never enters the universe, and the exclusion is invisible (no count, no lamp) — it just lowers stats.total's effective coverage. Combined with no FX handling, the universe boundary is defined by filename punctuation rather than an explicit exchange/country field.
nonScoring.fix: Filter on an explicit exchange/country field inside the payload (or a maintained suffix list) rather than 'contains a dot'. If filename convention must stay, special-case known dotted US class shares. Emit a count of files excluded by this rule so the universe boundary is auditable.

nonScoring.title: Durability source-select trusts revQYoYsec by length only (>=4) — it does not isFinite/null-filter inside the window before median/drawdown, and mixes the SEC-quarterly path with an annual fallback without recording window provenance per value
nonScoring.evidence: Line 143-144: `const revQYoYsec = arr(p.ftsQuarterly && p.ftsQuarterly.revQYoYsec); const gYoYDur = (revQYoYsec.length >= 4 ? revQYoYsec : gSeriesA).slice(0, DUR_W);`. arr() filters nulls globally, but the below-median loop at :149 re-checks isFinite per element — acknowledging the window may still contain non-finite values — yet durMed=median(gYoYDur) at :145 already consumed them via median()'s own filter, so durMed and durDD are computed over potentially different element counts than durCountBelow reports.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: durCountBelow / durWinN are surfaced as Re-Court disclosure fields (court-score.js:261 short-durability-window lamp), but they can disagree with the actual n used for durMed/durDD when the window holds non-finite entries, making the disclosed window size subtly wrong for borderline names (ALAB 7Q / ARM 8Q are explicitly called out).
nonScoring.fix: Filter the window to finite values once up front (`const gW = gYoYDur.filter(Number.isFinite)`) and compute durMed, durDD, durCountBelow, durWinN all from that single cleaned array so the disclosed window size matches the math. Comment: '// single cleaned window so disclosed durWinN matches the n used in median/drawdown'.

nonScoring.title: Lazy `trends` getter captures wrong ticker's history when stockDataMap dedup collides on duplicate tickers
nonScoring.evidence: Line 120: `const tickerHist = methodHistory[ticker] || {};` then line 128 inside the getter: `tr[m.id] = Trend.computeTrend(tickerHist[m.id] || [], m.thresholdOp);`. The getter closes over `tickerHist`, which is `methodHistory[ticker]`. `ticker` is derived on line 90 as `(stock.meta && stock.meta.ticker) || file.replace(/\.json$/, '')`. If two snapshot files resolve to the SAME ticker (e.g. `BRK-B.json` and a re-listed `BRK.B.json`, or a dual-listing where meta.ticker is identical), BOTH rows get a `trends` getter but they are distinct row objects — yet the matrix/top-picks de-dup (`stockDataMap[r.ticker]` line 378-379, and the matrix renders all rows) means the second row silently overwrites the first in STOCK_DATA_MAP while both still render as separate `<tr data-ticker=...>`. The modal/pc-filter then reads ONE ticker's data for two visually distinct rows. Trends are correct per-row, but the modal lookup is keyed only by ticker so the collision surfaces wrong per-row detail.
nonScoring.why_it_matters: Yahoo tickers are not guaranteed unique across snapshot files (class-share suffixes, ADR vs local listing, refresh-universe churn). A silent overwrite means the dashboard shows row A's name/rank with row B's method results in the modal — a data-integrity defect that is invisible (no error, no log) and corrupts exactly the 'why did this rank here' explanation Karl relies on.

nonScoring.title: Pass-count per method computed twice over the full M×N universe (renderHTML + main), result of first pass discarded

nonScoring.title: Leaderboard prof-state badge dereferences `state[0]` without guarding that `state` is a non-empty string

The guard stops at `ps.components` — it then indexes `ps.components.state[0]`. nonScoring.title: Matrix table ranks over ALL rows (incl. DataGuard-disqualified) while every other ranked surface ranks over discoveryRows — asymmetric attrition

If disqualified stocks should be visible-but-flagged in the Matrix, mark them (e.g. a 'DQ' badge) rather than silently mixing them into the ranking; if they should be excluded like everywhere else, sort/slice `matrixRanked` from `discoveryRows`. nonScoring.title: Division by `rows.length` with no zero-guard — empty snapshots dir yields NaN%/Infinity in sector + header output

nonScoring.title: `||` fallback on ticker treats a falsy-but-valid `meta.ticker` as missing (latent falsy-coalescing bug)

nonScoring.title: methodHistory fallback to alert-state only fires when sidecar yields ZERO keys — a partially-populated sidecar permanently masks legacy history

inUntouched.title: Windows reserved-name guard misses reserved stems that contain non-alphanumerics and the bare 'COM0'/extension-suffix cases; also fails the dot-as-first-char case
inUntouched.evidence: `const sanitized = String(ticker).replace(/[^A-Z0-9.-]/gi,'_'); const stem = sanitized.split('.')[0]; if (WINDOWS_RESERVED.test(stem)) return '_'+sanitized+'.json';` with `WINDOWS_RESERVED = /^(CON|PRN|AUX|NUL|COM[1-9]|LPT[1-9])$/i`. Two gaps: (1) the stem is taken as `split('.')[0]`, so a ticker like `CON_X` (a space/slash in the source ticker becomes `_`, giving stem `CON_X`) is NOT matched and is written as `CON_X.json` — but Windows only reserves the *exact* device names, so `CON_X` is actually safe; the real miss is the opposite: Windows ALSO reserves the device name when it appears as the full base name regardless of extension, which is handled, BUT it does NOT reserve `COM0`/`LPT0` — fine. (2) The genuinely missing modern reserved names: Windows also reserves `CONIN$`, `CONOUT$`, and on recent Windows the superscript COM/LPT digits, but more practically a ticker that is *only* a dot or starts with a dot (e.g. a malformed `.DE`) yields stem `''`, regex fails, file `.DE.json` — a hidden dotfile on POSIX and an odd name on Windows.
inUntouched.why_it_matters: This is the same class as the original CON.DE / Continental AG bug (Tag 134) that motivated the helper. The guard is a denylist of exact names; any ticker whose sanitised stem is a reserved device name written WITHOUT the helper-known form silently fails to write on Windows, breaking `git checkout`/`git pull` for Karl's Windows box and dropping that ticker's snapshot. Because the constraint forbids hardcoded ticker exclusions, the guard itself is the right place to harden.
inUntouched.fix: Tighten the guard rather than excluding tickers: after computing `stem`, also strip a trailing/leading dot and reject empty stems by prefixing `_`; and treat a stem that is empty or that case-insensitively equals a reserved name as reserved. Add the `CONIN$`/`CONOUT$` forms to WINDOWS_RESERVED. Each change carries a comment naming the failure mode: '// prevents un-writable snapshot on Windows (git checkout breaks) for reserved/empty stem'. Keep the regex anchored.

inUntouched.title: writeJsonAtomic serialises with JSON.stringify and no replacer guard — NaN/Infinity silently become null, corrupting numeric state files written through the 'safe' path

JSON.stringify converts NaN, Infinity and -Infinity to the literal `null`, and drops `undefined`-valued keys. This helper is the atomic writer used by fitness/measure.js:250 (`writeJsonAtomic(outFile, output)`) for computed fitness output, and the same JSON.stringify path is used implicitly by every writeFileAtomic caller that does `JSON.stringify(...)` upstream (e.g. snapshot-picks, check-pull-stats). Because this is the designated single-source-of-truth writer, a guard here protects every caller at once.

Although that step is continue-on-error, a throw here means the universe is never refreshed — new IPOs/mid-caps stop entering, and over time the universe stagnates (the asymmetric-attrition / survivorship concern), while the failure is masked by continue-on-error and only the downstream 'size < 200' floor (:148) would catch a catastrophic case, not a no-op. inUntouched.fix: Guard the maps: `wlRaw.stocks.map(s => s.ticker).filter(Boolean).map(t => t.toUpperCase())` for the Set, skip ticker-less entries when building newTickers, and make the sort null-safe (`(a.ticker||'').localeCompare(b.ticker||'')`). Comment the failure mode (one bad row → frozen universe).

inUntouched.title: Synchronous busy/Atomics.wait sleep inside the Windows rename-retry loop blocks the event loop for up to 380ms per contended write during the pull
inUntouched.evidence: _sleepSync (line 70) uses `Atomics.wait` (or a `while (Date.now() < end)` busy-spin fallback) and is called from _renameWithRetry (line 93) for each of RENAME_RETRY_DELAYS_MS = [10,20,50,100,200] (sum 380ms) on Windows EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES. pull-yahoo.js writes one snapshot per ticker through writeFileAtomic (lines 1664, 2156, 2216, 2284, etc.) across the whole universe.
inUntouched.why_it_matters: On Karl's Windows box, OneDrive sync + AV scanners are exactly the handle-holders this retry was built for (the module comment says so). During the multi-hour pull, every contended rename can block the single thread for up to 380ms synchronously — and because writeFileAtomic is intentionally sync, this stalls the async Yahoo fetch pipeline too, not just the write. Across a large universe with frequent OneDrive contention this is a real, if modest, contributor to the 14.6h pull wall-clock. Low severity because correctness is preserved and the per-file cost is bounded.
inUntouched.fix: Keep the sync contract (callers rely on it) but consider: (a) writing snapshots to a non-OneDrive-synced temp/staging dir and moving in bulk after the pull, removing the dominant contention source; or (b) trimming the retry ladder on Windows (the [100,200] tail rarely helps for sub-50ms transient locks). If neither, document the worst-case stall. Do not convert to async (would force a large caller refactor against the module's stated design).

inUntouched.title: Between-batch sleep is a fixed 300ms that ignores how long the batch's own Promise.all took — rate-limit pacing is the tail latency, not the gap
inUntouched.evidence: Lines 39-45: `for (... batchStart += CONCURRENCY) { const batch = wl.stocks.slice(...); await Promise.all(batch.map(s => processOne(s).catch(()=>{}))); if (batchStart + CONCURRENCY < wl.stocks.length) await sleep(300); }`. The 300ms is added AFTER awaiting the whole batch, so when a batch returns fast (cache hits / fast network) 15 concurrent quoteSummary calls fire, then only 300ms passes before the next 15 — bursts of 15 every ~300ms+batchtime.
inUntouched.why_it_matters: Earnings pulls hit the same Yahoo Cloudflare edge that forced PULL_CONCURRENCY and EARNINGS_CONCURRENCY down to 8 (daily-pull.yml:42,465 — the Tag 215f lesson). A fixed post-batch gap with concurrency 15 (default :24) or even 8 can still micro-burst and trigger 429s, which are then swallowed by the per-item empty catch (:36) so the calendar silently under-populates. Lower-severity because errors are tolerated, but it caps reliable coverage.
inUntouched.fix: Either lower default EARNINGS_CONCURRENCY to match the workflow's 8, or pace by elapsed time: record batch start, sleep `max(0, minInterval - elapsed)`. Add the rate-limit-boundary failure-mode comment.

inUntouched.title: marketCap kept via `(allTickers.get(sym).marketCap || 0) < mcap` and capped via `b[1].marketCap - a[1].marketCap` — non-finite/NaN marketCap from a source poisons the dedupe and the rank-sort

At cap time :390 `withMcap.sort((a,b) => b[1].marketCap - a[1].marketCap)` after filtering `v.marketCap != null && v.marketCap > 0` (:386) — that filter screens null but NOT NaN (NaN != null is true, NaN > 0 is false, so NaN rows actually fall into withoutMcap — acceptable), however any Infinity from a bad source would sort to the top and crowd out real names.

A source emitting Infinity/huge bogus mcap would rank-sort to the front of withMcap and consume top slots under the MAX_UNIVERSE cap, displacing legitimate large caps — a silent universe-composition bias.
inUntouched.fix: Normalize on ingest: when storing marketCap, coerce with `Number.isFinite(m) && m>0 ? m : null`. Then the existing null-bucket logic handles it correctly. One-line guard at each `allTickers.set`.

inUntouched.title: BENCHMARKS are unshift-ed into the in-memory watchlist every run but the watchlist is read-only here — harmless now, but couples benchmark identity to ticker-string equality and will silently double-insert if yahoo_symbol ever differs from ticker
inUntouched.evidence: Lines 57-58: `for (const b of BENCHMARKS) { if (!wl.stocks.find(s => s.ticker === b.ticker)) wl.stocks.unshift(b); }`. A duplicate SPY would get processed twice and the second pass is a redundant Yahoo call.

inUntouched.title: todaysSnapshot keyed close uses adjclose but the per-day prices/<date>.json `asOf` is calendar `today`, not the actual trading date — re-introduces the weekend phantom-date the history fix (Tag 231a-3) deliberately removed

inTouched.title: extractStocksArray and detectShape are exported but have zero importers — dead public surface

inTouched.title: Insurance industries misclassified as FINTECH; keyword branch swallows insurers before any insurance-specific or sector check
inTouched.evidence: Line 89: `if (ind.includes('fintech') || ind.includes('payment') || ind.includes('insurance')) return SUB_PROFILES.FINTECH;`. This is a silent scoring-quality cap — exactly the kind of structural ceiling implied by 'screener at ~20% of potential'. It is data-driven (no ticker hardcoding) so it is in-bounds to fix.
inTouched.fix: Route insurance to a more economically-honest bucket. Minimal fix without adding a profile: move insurers to BANK (closest balance-sheet-driven peer set) or FINTECH only for 'insurance brokers' (fee-based) while sending carriers elsewhere. Cleaner fix: add an INSURANCE sub-profile to SUB_PROFILES and branch on `ind.includes('insurance')` before line 89. Comment: '// prevents insurer float/combined-ratio economics from polluting the FINTECH peer-median used in sector-relative scoring'.

inTouched.title: TICKER_SUBPROFILE_MAP is a hardcoded ticker override table baked into a 'pure deterministic classifier' — and it is exported but unused, so overrides silently depend on Yahoo meta.ticker exact-casing
inTouched.evidence: Lines 33-56 hardcode ~22 ticker->profile overrides (NVDA->HARDWARE, META->MARKETPLACE, AAPL->HARDWARE, etc.). classifySubProfile reads `const ticker = (stock.meta && stock.meta.ticker || '').toUpperCase().trim();` (line 67) then `TICKER_SUBPROFILE_MAP[ticker]`. The map has both `RHM` and `RHM.DE` (lines 40-41) — duplicating the override for the regional suffix, which means any *other* dual-listed ticker (e.g. a US ADR vs local line) silently falls through to the heuristic for one of its two forms. If a snapshot stores the ticker with an exchange suffix (`META` vs `META.US`) or Yahoo changes casing, the override misses and the stock reverts to the heuristic — e.g. META falls out of MARKETPLACE into... the heuristic, which for 'Internet Content & Information' has no explicit branch and could land OTHER. This is a silent, per-ticker classification flip. (2) The map is a maintenance liability: a hand-curated allowlist of megacaps inside a 'pure, deterministic' library is the kind of thing that drifts as Yahoo industries change, and the comment on NVDA even admits 'User-Diskussion offen'. (3) Dead export widens surface.
inTouched.fix: Do not remove the overrides (they encode real judgement calls) but: (a) drop TICKER_SUBPROFILE_MAP from module.exports since no one imports it; (b) normalise the lookup key to strip the exchange suffix (match on `ticker.split('.')[0]`) so RHM and RHM.DE need only one entry and dual-listings are robust — comment: '// prevents override-miss when Yahoo returns the suffixed ticker form, which silently reverts the stock to the keyword heuristic'; (c) consider moving the table to a data/config file long-term so the classifier stays pure. No hardcoded *exclusions* are involved, so this respects the constraint.

inTouched.title: Comment/code mismatch on Discord retry_after units; relies on body field being seconds while the comment claims milliseconds
inTouched.evidence: Line 116 comment: '429: honor retry-after (header in seconds, body in milliseconds).' Line 126: `if (j && Number.isFinite(j.retry_after)) waitMs = Math.max(waitMs, Math.ceil(j.retry_after * 1000));`. The code multiplies the JSON body's `retry_after` by 1000 (seconds->ms), which is correct for the actual Discord API (v8+ returns `retry_after` as a float in SECONDS, not ms). So the CODE is right but the COMMENT is wrong — the body is seconds, not milliseconds.
inTouched.why_it_matters: The behaviour is currently correct (×1000 of a seconds value gives ms), so no live bug. But the misleading comment is a trap: a future maintainer trusting 'body in milliseconds' could 'fix' the apparent ×1000 by removing it, which would then under-wait by 1000× and reintroduce dropped 429 alerts under sustained rate-limiting — the exact failure F-230c-06 was added to prevent. Since picks-regression-check (the noisy-day burst path) depends on this, the latent foot-gun is worth removing.
inTouched.fix: Correct the comment to 'header in seconds (integer), body retry_after in seconds (float)'. No code change. This keeps the alert-durability guarantee legible.

inTouched.title: 429 retry consumes a loop iteration without counting toward a network-call budget; a 429+5xx mix can issue up to maxRetries+2 POSTs and a non-final 429 does not honor a body retry_after cap symmetrically
inTouched.evidence: On a non-final 429 the code computes waitMs (capped 10s), sleeps, and `continue`s WITHOUT decrementing any separate budget (line 149-150). On the final attempt it does an EXTRA honored sleep+post (lines 136-148). So the worst-case POST count is the loop body (attempts 0..maxRetries = 3 posts) PLUS the terminal honored retry (1 more) = up to 4 network POSTs for maxRetries=2. Separately, a non-final 429 reads the body via _jsonWithTimeout (line 125) only on... it does read it on every 429 including non-final — but the `waitMs = Math.min(waitMs, 10000)` cap (line 130) is applied before the final-attempt branch, so the terminal honored retry also respects the 10s cap; that part is fine.
inTouched.why_it_matters: This is defensive code for alert durability, so erring toward more retries is acceptable per the module's own rationale ('a true duplicate alert is far better than a missed one'). The only real concern is that the retry accounting is implicit: the loop variable doubles as both 'attempt index' and 'retry budget', so reasoning about the true maximum wall-clock (up to 3×timeout for posts + 2×10s sleeps + 1×500ms ≈ 35s) is non-obvious and could brush against a CI step timeout, the very thing the AbortController was added to bound. Low severity because each individual call is bounded.
inTouched.fix: No behavioural change required, but add a one-line comment documenting the worst-case wall-clock (POSTs + honored sleeps) so the CI-timeout interaction is explicit, OR introduce an explicit `maxWallClockMs` guard if Karl wants a hard ceiling. Leave the dedupe-friendly extra retry as-is.

inTouched.title: Keyed-map heuristic uses a strict majority test that can still misread a small mixed object, and silently yields shape 'object' with a synthetic ticker array
inTouched.evidence: Line 63: `const looksKeyedMap = keys.length > 0 && tickerLike.length * 2 > keys.length;` then line 65 returns `{ shape: 'object', stocks: keys.map(...) }`. For a tiny object like `{ AAPL: {...}, note: 'x' }` (2 keys, 1 ticker-like since 'note' is a string not object) -> tickerLike=1, 1*2=2 > 2 is false -> invalid (good). But `{ AAPL: {...}, MSFT: {...}, _meta: 'x' }` -> tickerLike=2, 2*2=4 > 3 true -> treated as keyed map, and `_meta` (string) is mapped to `{ ticker:'_meta', 0:'x'... }` via Object.assign of a string, injecting a junk synthetic stock.
inTouched.why_it_matters: The synthetic-array branch will faithfully convert EVERY key including non-ticker metadata keys once the majority test passes, because the map step (line 65) does not re-apply the TICKER_KEY_RE / typeof-object filter used to *detect* the shape. A stray metadata key on a legacy keyed-map watchlist becomes a phantom stock with a garbage ticker, which then flows into universeSize / drift-gate counts in check-pull-stats.js — subtly inflating the universe count the drift gate compares against. The keyed-map shape is 'long-retired' per the docstring, so exposure is low, but the asymmetry (detect with a filter, map without one) is a latent correctness gap.
inTouched.fix: When building the synthetic array, reuse the same predicate: `keys.filter(k => TICKER_KEY_RE.test(k) && raw[k] && typeof raw[k]==='object').map(k => Object.assign({ticker:k}, raw[k]))`. This guarantees the emitted stocks are exactly the ticker-like, object-valued keys that justified the 'object' classification — comment: '// prevents metadata keys on a legacy keyed-map from becoming phantom stocks that inflate the drift-gate universe count'.

inTouched.title: 13F tests mutate the REAL production cache (external-data/sec-13f-by-ticker.json) and run in CI — a crash/timeout in the stub→restore window leaves the 85KB production cache as a 1-entry stub
inTouched.evidence: const CACHE_PATH_13F = path.join(__dirname, 'external-data', 'sec-13f-by-ticker.json'); ... function _stubCache(obj){ _writeCacheRaw(JSON.stringify(obj)); inst13fModule._resetCacheForTests(); } and in each test: const orig=_readCacheRaw(); try{ _stubCache({...byTicker:{TESTCO:...}}); ... } finally { _restoreCache(orig); }. The path is the live cache: `ls external-data` shows sec-13f-by-ticker.json = 85173 bytes, present in the worktree. daily-pull.yml:88 runs `node tag28-tests.js` in that same worktree, and method-types.js:100 marks institutional-ownership-13f defaultActive:true, so the very next pipeline step reads this file.

That is a misdiagnosis: writeFileAtomic only makes a SINGLE write atomic. The real hazard is the test deliberately OVERWRITING production data with a 1-ticker stub and relying on a finally-block restore. If the Node process is SIGKILLed / hits the CI job timeout / OOMs while the stub is on disk (between _stubCache and _restoreCache), the 85KB smart-money cache is permanently replaced by {byTicker:{TESTCO:...}}. Every subsequent screener run then sees institutional-ownership-13f as not-computable for the entire universe (silent signal loss across ~all tickers) until the next 13F pull regenerates it — and daily-pull.yml has no 13F-regen step after the test. This is exactly the 'silently swallowed / non-atomic state' class the audit targets, made worse because it is self-inflicted by the test suite.
inTouched.fix: Do NOT touch the real cache path from tests. Inject the cache location instead of hardcoding it: give institutional-ownership-13f a setter (e.g. _setCachePathForTests) or have _evaluateWithCache(stock, cacheObj) like ICS._evaluateWithTxns / momModule already do. Point the tests at a path under os.tmpdir()/a tests/-local fixture file, or pass the stub object directly. This removes all production-file I/O from the suite and makes the writeFileAtomic plumbing unnecessary.

inTouched.title: _restoreCache(null) / _writeCacheRaw(null) call fs.unlinkSync on the real production cache — if the cache is momentarily absent at test start, the real file gets DELETED
inTouched.evidence: function _writeCacheRaw(s){ if (s == null){ try{ fs.unlinkSync(CACHE_PATH_13F); }catch(e){} return; } ... }  function _restoreCache(originalRaw){ if (originalRaw == null){ try{ fs.unlinkSync(CACHE_PATH_13F); }catch(e){} } else _writeCacheRaw(originalRaw); ... }. orig comes from _readCacheRaw() which returns null on ANY read error (catch(e){return null;}), not only 'file absent'.
inTouched.why_it_matters: _readCacheRaw swallows every error to null (transient EBUSY/locked file on Windows, a concurrent writer, a permissions blip). When orig===null for a transient reason, the test still stubs the cache, then 'restores' by UNLINKING the real 85KB production file. The deletion is also silently swallowed (catch(e){}). Combined with finding 01 this turns a flaky read into permanent data loss of a production artifact, with zero log output. unlinkSync on shared production state from a unit test is unjustifiable.
inTouched.fix: Eliminate per finding 01 (use a tmp/injected path so deleting it is harmless). If a real-path round-trip must stay, distinguish 'file genuinely absent' (fs.existsSync false) from 'read failed' and refuse to unlink on read-error; never unlink a production path from a test.

inTouched.title: Fixture-hash golden test self-heals a missing tests/fixture-hash.txt by writing it and returning PASS — a deleted/absent golden file silently disarms the score-aggregator regression guard in CI

On any runner where the file is absent, the golden test writes whatever the CURRENT code produces and reports PASS — so a real scoring regression introduced in the same commit is baselined as 'correct' and ships. A golden test that auto-adopts the observed output on a fresh checkout provides no protection exactly when you most need it. (The ALLOW_FIXTURE_CHANGE=1 path at 2803 is the intended escape hatch; the silent no-env path at 2809 should not exist.)

inTouched.title: Tests mutate shared module-level caches but reset without try/finally — a thrown assertion leaks stub state into later tests, making results order-dependent (false pass or false fail)
inTouched.evidence: The hand-rolled harness: function test(name,fn){ try{ fn(); ... } catch(e){ ... } }. price-momentum tests call momModule._resetCacheForTests() at the START only (line 1962/1975/1986) with no finally; the fixture-hash test uses Helpers._setMediansForTest then restores in a finally (2774/2795 — correct), but the 13F tests' inst13fModule._resetCacheForTests() inside _stubCache/_restoreCache runs only if those helpers are reached. There is no global afterEach reset.
inTouched.why_it_matters: momModule and inst13fModule hold a process-global _cache. If an assertion throws between a reset and the next reset (e.g. price-momentum PASS test fails on barsUsed), the cache populated from the failing test's stub persists into the next test, which can then read stale data and either spuriously pass (masking a real defect) or spuriously fail (false alarm). Reset-at-start-without-finally is fragile: the suite's correctness depends on every test fully completing. This is the classic shared-mutable-state test-isolation bug; it also makes the fixture-hash determinism the suite advertises unreliable if a medians/cache reset is skipped.
inTouched.fix: Reset all injectable caches in a finally per test (or add an afterEach hook to the harness that calls each module's _resetCacheForTests). Better: stop relying on module-global caches in tests — pass state explicitly via the _evaluateWith* injection seams that already exist for ICS.

inTouched.title: Harness cannot detect async failures or hangs: test() only catches synchronous throws, and exit code is derived solely from a sync `failed` counter with no per-test timeout
inTouched.evidence: function test(name, fn){ try{ fn(); console.log(' V '+name); passed++; } catch(e){ ... failed++; } }  ... process.exit(failed > 0 ? 1 : 0);  — fn is invoked synchronously; a returned Promise rejection would be unobserved, and an infinite loop in any method has no timeout.
inTouched.why_it_matters: All current tests are synchronous, but the suite tests the data pipeline whose modules increasingly touch fs and could become async. Any future async method (or an accidentally-async assertion) would always report PASS because the rejection lands after process.exit. And because tag28-tests.js is a CI pre-pull GUARD (daily-pull.yml:88, 'Schützt gegen production-Schäden'), a hang means the daily pull stalls with no signal rather than failing fast. A guard you trust to protect production should fail closed on async errors and on timeout.
inTouched.fix: Detect Promise returns from fn and await/flag them; install a process-level unhandledRejection handler that bumps `failed`; wrap the whole run with a watchdog timer (or migrate to node:test / a real runner that handles async + timeouts natively).

inTouched.title: FX conversion test asserts a hardcoded USD range tied to mutable live fx-rates.json — couples a 'unit' test to external market data and will false-fail CI when TWD moves outside 0.020–0.050

inTouched.title: 2825-line god test-file with a hand-rolled runner conflates ~50 module unit tests, a CI fixture-hash golden, and live production-file I/O in one process
inTouched.evidence: Single file, 155971 bytes, one shared `passed/failed` counter, ~250 inline test() calls spanning rule-of-40 through Buffett-criteria, plus _computeFixtureHash (2763) and real-cache I/O (1859). No test runner; assertions are ad-hoc throws.

It also caps maintainability — adding a method means editing a 2825-line file, and a single early throw/exit can skip the fixture-hash golden entirely (it is the LAST test, line 2799, so any earlier process.exit or crash silently skips the one check that guards scoring). If the intent is strictly 'one *threshold* miss', then additionally exclude any stock with incomputable MUSTs from the panel rather than silently ignoring them. But the mode-eval gate uses `const mode_eval_total = stocks.length * Object.keys(SM.MODES).length;` (line 1353) — excluding parse-error files — and `mode_eval_rate = n_mode_eval_errors / mode_eval_total`.

More importantly, modeEvalErrors are only incremented for stocks that *survived* loading and the outer try (line 132); stocks killed by the outer per-stock catch (line 138-141) never enter the mode loop, so the numerator omits whole-stock failures while the denominator assumes every loaded stock ran every mode. A wave of stocks throwing in Runner.evaluateStock inflates _pipelineFailures (caught by gate 1) but artificially depresses mode_eval_rate, which could mask a *correlated* mode-level break that only manifests on the stocks that did evaluate.
inTouched.fix: Compute mode_eval_total from the count of stocks that actually reached the mode loop (results.length * modeCount), or from (stocks.length - perStockFailures) * modeCount, and keep the denominators consistent with the per-stock gate. inTouched.title: Mojibake/accent folding in dedupe norm() is a fragile byte-level hack that only covers UTF-8 lead-byte artifacts, not real Unicode
inTouched.evidence: `if (/[^\x00-\x7f]/.test(str)) { str = str.replace(/[Ã©¨ª«³²´¶¡ ¢¤]/g, function (c) { var cp = c.codePointAt(0); if (cp === 0xb3 ...) return 'o'; ... return 'e'; }); }` (lines 212-218). The character class is a hand-picked set of Latin-1 bytes plus the 0xC3 mojibake lead byte; the comment admits it maps 'the lone mojibake lead byte'.
inTouched.why_it_matters: Real accented company names (e.g. 'Saint-Gobain', 'Münchener', 'Nestlé' stored as proper Unicode é U+00E9) are NOT in the class — only the specific mis-decoded byte sequences are handled. So genuinely-encoded foreign names and mojibake names normalize differently, meaning the same company under two encodings produces two keys and is NOT deduped, while unrelated names sharing a stripped stem ARE deduped (see A-report-modes-02). The dedupe key quality directly bounds universe integrity, and this approach silently degrades as data sources change encoding.
inTouched.fix: Replace the byte-level hack with String.prototype.normalize('NFKD').replace(/\p{Diacritic}/gu,'') to fold all diacritics uniformly, and fix the upstream encoding so mojibake never reaches the snapshot in the first place. This makes the dedupe key encoding-independent. (Behavioral change to dedupe — pair with the keying fix in A-report-modes-02 and verify against a name-collision fixture.)

Minor UX defect but it makes the headline mcap filter (the screener's most-used control) frustrating, contributing to the tool feeling under-finished.

inTouched.title: Worker-pool rate-limit sleep is per-worker, not global — effective request rate is concurrency × the intended rate, defeating the anti-429 throttle
inTouched.evidence: runWorkerPool: each worker independently does `if (myIdx + concurrency < stocks.length) await _sleep(sleepMs)` (line 2252) after every ticker. With CONCURRENCY workers each sleeping rateLimitMs between its own pulls, aggregate throughput is ~concurrency/rateLimitMs req/s. The comment at 2232 even states this: 'With 20 workers and rateLimitMs=1500ms per worker, throughput is ~13 tickers/sec.' So the 1500ms 'rate limit' is NOT a global request spacing.
inTouched.why_it_matters: The whole point of --rate-limit ≥1500ms (documented at file top, line 19, as the defense against Yahoo 403/429 blocking) is global request spacing. Because the sleep is per-worker, raising PULL_CONCURRENCY silently multiplies the real hit-rate against Yahoo's Cloudflare edge. This is the structural mechanism behind the documented 7,210 rate-limit failures in Run #107 (referenced at line 1342) — operators lower concurrency and raise backoff to compensate, but the knob they think throttles globally does not. It caps the 14.6h pull's reliability and forces conservative concurrency.
inTouched.fix: Introduce a single shared rate-gate (e.g. a module-level `nextSlotAt` timestamp the workers advance atomically, or a token-bucket/leaky-bucket limiter) so that the MINIMUM spacing between consecutive Yahoo requests across ALL workers is rateLimitMs — decoupled from concurrency. Then concurrency controls parallelism of in-flight requests while the gate controls issue rate. Keep the per-worker sleep removed to avoid double-counting.

inTouched.title: Shared `idx++` work-stealing counter is technically a read-modify-write race (benign under current single-threaded event loop, fragile if any await is inserted before the increment)

inTouched.why_it_matters: It works now, but it is a latent trap: any future refactor that makes index acquisition async (e.g. awaiting a shared rate-gate as recommended in finding 01, or a priority queue) would let two workers read the same `idx`, double-pulling one ticker and skipping another — silent universe attrition that no test would catch. Worth a one-line guard comment naming the invariant.
inTouched.fix: Leave the logic but add a comment that index acquisition MUST stay synchronous (no await between `idx` read and increment), or switch to a shared async-safe queue (`stocks.shift()` style or an explicit cursor object) before adding any await to the acquisition path. Failure mode prevented: duplicate/skipped tickers from a future async work-steal.

inTouched.title: price-only and full-pull scale marketCap by an FX trading-factor but never scale snap.price.regularMarketPrice on the full pull, while price-only DOES scale price — the two pull modes leave price in inconsistent currency units across refreshes
inTouched.evidence: Price-only path multiplies BOTH price and mcap by tradingFactor: `existing.price.regularMarketPrice = q.regularMarketPrice * tradingFactor` (1606) and `existing.marketCap.value = q.marketCap * tradingFactor` (1616). But _convertSnapshotToUSD (full pull) explicitly does NOT scale price — comment at 411-414: 'We intentionally do NOT scale snap.price here … price stays in trading currency by design'. The full-pull mapper never even builds snap.price (confirmed by the NEW-2/NEW-3 note at 349-355).
inTouched.why_it_matters: For an ADR/foreign-listed ticker, a full pull produces a snapshot whose marketCap is USD-converted but whose (absent or trading-ccy) price is unconverted, while the very next day's price-only refresh writes a USD-converted regularMarketPrice. Any consumer that reads price.regularMarketPrice (e.g. analyst-upside vs currentPrice, per-share ratios) gets a value whose currency depends on which pull mode last touched the file — a silent mixed-unit field that flips daily. This is exactly the class of FX-normalization bug that corrupts downstream ratios for non-USD names.
inTouched.fix: Make price handling symmetric and explicit: either (a) always store price in USD in both paths (scale price by tradingFactor on full pull too, and document it), or (b) never store a converted price and have price-only also leave regularMarketPrice in trading currency, recording tradingCurrency in meta. Pick one invariant, assert it on write, and have consumers read meta.tradingCurrency to interpret price. Comment must name the failure mode: 'price-field currency drifts between full-pull and price-only refreshes'.

inTouched.title: _priceOnlyUpdate throws AFTER mutating `existing` in memory but the snapshot is only re-persisted on success — on the mcap-floor branch it unlinks the file, otherwise a thrown price-only falls through to a full pull, but the in-memory mutation of the shared parsed object can leak if reused
inTouched.evidence: `_priceOnlyUpdate` receives `preParsed` (the object parsed once in processOne at 1688) and mutates it in place: sets existing.meta.asOf (1562), existing.price.regularMarketPrice (1606), existing.marketCap.value (1616) BEFORE the throw points at 1583/1626. The same `_parsedSnapshot` object is then NOT re-used after a price-only failure (full pull rebuilds canonical from scratch), so today it is harmless — but the mutation-before-validation ordering is unsafe by construction.
inTouched.why_it_matters: The price-only function partially applies a new asOf and a scaled price/mcap to the shared parsed object, then can throw (non-USD-without-fxRate at 1583, or mcap-below-floor at 1626). Because processOne discards the object on the full-pull fall-through, the corruption is currently contained, but the contract is brittle: any caller that retries with the same preParsed object, or any future code that reads _parsedSnapshot after a failed price-only, would see a half-updated snapshot with a fresh asOf but stale-source price. The fresh asOf is the dangerous part — it would make a corrupt snapshot look freshly pulled.
inTouched.fix: Compute the new values into locals first, validate (fx-rate present, mcap ≥ floor) BEFORE any mutation of `existing`, and only then apply. Treat the parsed object as immutable until validation passes. Comment naming the failure mode: 'half-applied price-only mutation with refreshed asOf masquerading as a clean snapshot'.

inTouched.title: Insider `shares` raw-envelope unwrap is inconsistent with _y(): reads only top-level `.raw`, so a yahoo-finance2 already-unwrapped number vs a {raw,fmt} object are handled by different code paths, and a nested/absent raw yields 0

inTouched.title: FX `scale()` applies the reporting `factor` to balance-sheet/annual rows including share-count-like or unit-less fields that slip past the annualShares guard (e.g. annualBalance has no share field, but timeseries/annual maps blindly multiply every numeric key)

inTouched.title: Absence-as-zero debt summing `(std || 0) + (ltd || 0)` treats a legitimately reported 0 identically to a missing line, and the `|| 0` falsy fallback also collapses a real 0 debt into the 'present' branch — the _debtPartial flag can mislabel a genuine zero-debt company

The null-vs-present decision uses `== null` (correct), but the SUM uses `std || 0` / `ltd || 0` — a real reported debt of exactly 0 is indistinguishable from null in the addition (both contribute 0, which is fine arithmetically) BUT a company that reports std=0 (true zero current debt) and ltd=null is flagged `_debtPartial` with reason 'no-long-term-debt', conflating 'Yahoo omitted the line' with 'company has long-term debt we couldn't read'. The brief explicitly calls out '|| 0 falsy bugs (0 legitimately valid)'.

The reason string (no-current-debt vs no-long-term-debt) is consumed by downstream leverage methods to size understatement. Because `== null` is used for the partial decision this is mostly correct, but the residual issue is that a TRUE zero in one leg with a missing other leg is reported as partial-understated when it may be complete — over-flagging leverage uncertainty on genuinely low-debt names. The asymmetry between the `== null` partial-check and the `|| 0` sum is the smell.
inTouched.fix: Keep the deliberate absence-as-zero sum (changing it is out of scope per constraints), but distinguish reported-zero from missing in the _debtPartial reason: flag partial only when the missing leg is `== null` AND the present leg is > 0 (i.e. there is actual debt that the missing leg could materially add to). inTouched.title: annualShares fallback chain can mix share-count bases across years: primary tries dilutedAverageShares per-year, and ONLY if the ENTIRE array is all-null falls back to basicAverageShares/ordinarySharesNumber — so a partially-populated diluted series is never backfilled from basic, leaving year-gaps

A mid-window null produces a gap that those methods treat as incomputable for that span, OR (worse) if they index-align, pairs a diluted-basis count against a basic-basis count from a sibling array. inTouched.fix: Build annualShares per-year with an explicit basis preference and record which basis each year used (diluted > basic > ordinary), backfilling per-year rather than all-or-nothing, and store a parallel basis tag so consumers can reject mixed-basis spans. inTouched.title: No FX/currency normalization anywhere — revenue, GP, FCF, RPO are taken raw from Yahoo, so scale gates, scaleRevM, mega-cap flag, rpoToRev and cross-sectional medians mix USD and non-USD reporters
inTouched.evidence: court-screen.js:100 `revLatest = revA[0]`, :127 `scaleRevM = revLatest / 1e6`, with no currency field read from payload. court-score.js:222 gates membership on `log10(Math.max(m.scaleRevM, 1))` against scaleLog.c=log10(50)/2.0; :116 MEGACAP_REVM=15000 ($15B) compared to scaleRevM; A2 rpoToRev (court-score.js:213) and rpoLatest credibility (cred(), :121, floor $50M/$300M) are all USD-assumed. Yahoo reports financials in the issuer's native currency (e.g. ILA, EUR, JPY, KRW).

The cross-sectional median/MAD per bucket is computed over a currency-mixed universe, contaminating every z-score. The membership pre-filter even has a comment about asset-light/scale anchors but no FX guard. This is a classic survivorship/normalization data-integrity hole that caps cross-sectional validity.
inTouched.fix: Read the financialCurrency from the Yahoo payload and convert revenue/GP/FCF/RPO/scale to a single reporting currency (USD) via an as-of FX table before any gate or anchor. If currency is missing, flag the name (lamp) rather than silently treating it as USD. Comment the conversion site with the failure mode it prevents (currency-driven scale/mega-cap misclassification).

inTouched.title: MAD==0 silently collapses an axis to neutral for the whole bucket — when >50% of members share a value (common after winsorize/rounding), every member's z on that axis becomes 0
inTouched.evidence: sAxis line 33: `if (raw == null || med == null || m == null || m === 0) return 0; // neutral` — m is the MAD. mad() (line 26) returns 0 whenever the median absolute deviation is 0, i.e. a majority of values are identical. growth/accel are winsorized (court-screen.js via clip) and all values are round()-ed to 4 decimals, increasing tie frequency. When MAD=0 the axis contributes a flat w*(0+1)/2 to every member — it stops discriminating entirely, with no lamp.
inTouched.why_it_matters: An axis can go fully inert for a bucket (e.g. a small bucket where opMargin or roicMinusWacc clusters) and no diagnostic is emitted — the score looks normal but is effectively (n-1)-dimensional. Quietly caps discrimination and is invisible to the operator, unlike the many other conditions that raise lamps.
inTouched.fix: When stats[ax.key].mad===0 (or n below a floor), emit a per-bucket 'axis-inert(<name>)' lamp/diagnostic and consider falling back to a scaled-IQR or a tiny epsilon so ties still order by sign. Comment: '// MAD=0 means the axis is non-discriminating for this bucket — surface it instead of silently neutralizing'.

inTouched.title: No isFinite guard on membership M or final score — a NaN from any axis (e.g. malformed maRpo record feeding _a2, or scaleRevM<=0) propagates to score and corrupts the sort
inTouched.evidence: Line 223 `const M = mg * mGM * mSc;` and line 241 `m.score = Math.max(0, 100 * core - pDil - pAuth)`. Math.max(0, NaN) === NaN. core accumulates `ax.w * (s + 1) / 2` where s for a2Forward is `m._a2` (line 232), computed by computeA2Forward from snapshot fields with no final isFinite clamp (lines 123-130 can produce NaN if cred() gets a non-numeric base or sAxis gets a non-finite raw that slips the null check). members.sort((a,b)=>b.score-a.score) at line 307 with any NaN score yields an undefined ordering.
inTouched.why_it_matters: A single bad snapshot row can silently scramble the entire bucket ranking (NaN comparisons make Array.sort order implementation-defined), and a NaN membership mis-buckets In/Borderline/Out. The codebase guards null carefully elsewhere but never guards the non-finite result of the arithmetic.
inTouched.fix: Clamp at the boundaries: `if (!isFinite(M)) M = 0;` before membershipClass; `m.score = isFinite(m.score) ? m.score : 0;` after line 241 (and after the reweight at line 299), and isFinite-guard computeA2Forward's return. Comment: '// NaN score from a malformed snapshot row must not scramble the sort'.

inTouched.title: Dedupe fingerprint can still drop a distinct issuer: round()-ed growth/fcfMargin (4 dp) plus integer scaleRevM means two different companies sharing those 4 values collide, and the kept record is chosen by Map iteration order (non-deterministic w.r.t. which issuer survives)

It is better than before but still a silent attrition path with order-dependent outcome.

inTouched.title: ROIC proxy hardcodes a 0.79 tax-shield and Schritt 2 applies a single flat WACC=0.09 to every name — the A4 ROIC-WACC axis is effectively a ROIC rank with a constant offset, not a spread
inTouched.evidence: court-screen.js:181 `roicProxy = (opA[0] * 0.79) / ic` (0.79 = assumed 21% tax, no per-name tax data). court-score.js:106 `const WACC = 0.09; // [TODO-CAL] grober Proxy für A4` and :192 `m.roicMinusWacc = c.roicProxy - WACC`. Subtracting the same constant from every name's ROIC before cross-sectional z (median/MAD) cancels out — the median shifts by exactly 0.09 too — so roicMinusWacc ranks identically to roicProxy alone.
inTouched.why_it_matters: The A4 'ROIC minus WACC' axis advertises an economic-spread read but, being a constant subtraction ahead of a median-centered z, contributes nothing beyond raw ROIC ordering. Effort/weight (w=0.078) is spent on a relabeled ROIC. Caps the analytic value of the SaaS formula's quality block.
inTouched.fix: Either drop the WACC subtraction (it is a no-op pre-z) and label the axis honestly as ROIC, or make WACC name-specific (size/beta/leverage proxy) so the spread actually varies cross-sectionally. Tag [TODO-CAL] resolution with the failure mode: 'constant WACC pre-z is a no-op; A4 must vary by name to add signal'.

inTouched.title: Cache file filter uses a fragile regex to mean 'no exchange suffix' — any US ticker containing a dot (BRK.B, BF.B) is excluded, and the double-extension intent is opaque

Intent is to keep no-suffix US names (drop FOO.L, FOO.TO). But class-share US tickers legitimately contain a dot (BRK.B, BF.B, HEI.A), so their cache files are silently skipped.
inTouched.why_it_matters: Asymmetric survivorship at ingestion: a whole class of legitimate US issuers never enters the universe, and the exclusion is invisible (no count, no lamp) — it just lowers stats.total's effective coverage. Combined with no FX handling, the universe boundary is defined by filename punctuation rather than an explicit exchange/country field.
inTouched.fix: Filter on an explicit exchange/country field inside the payload (or a maintained suffix list) rather than 'contains a dot'. If filename convention must stay, special-case known dotted US class shares. Emit a count of files excluded by this rule so the universe boundary is auditable.

inTouched.title: Durability source-select trusts revQYoYsec by length only (>=4) — it does not isFinite/null-filter inside the window before median/drawdown, and mixes the SEC-quarterly path with an annual fallback without recording window provenance per value
