inTouched.fix: Filter the window to finite values once up front (`const gW = gYoYDur.filter(Number.isFinite)`) and compute durMed, durDD, durCountBelow, durWinN all from that single cleaned array so the disclosed window size matches the math. Comment: '// single cleaned window so disclosed durWinN matches the n used in median/drawdown'.

inTouched.title: Lazy `trends` getter captures wrong ticker's history when stockDataMap dedup collides on duplicate tickers
inTouched.evidence: Line 120: `const tickerHist = methodHistory[ticker] || {};` then line 128 inside the getter: `tr[m.id] = Trend.computeTrend(tickerHist[m.id] || [], m.thresholdOp);`. The getter closes over `tickerHist`, which is `methodHistory[ticker]`. `ticker` is derived on line 90 as `(stock.meta && stock.meta.ticker) || file.replace(/\.json$/, '')`. If two snapshot files resolve to the SAME ticker (e.g. `BRK-B.json` and a re-listed `BRK.B.json`, or a dual-listing where meta.ticker is identical), BOTH rows get a `trends` getter but they are distinct row objects — yet the matrix/top-picks de-dup (`stockDataMap[r.ticker]` line 378-379, and the matrix renders all rows) means the second row silently overwrites the first in STOCK_DATA_MAP while both still render as separate `<tr data-ticker=...>`. The modal/pc-filter then reads ONE ticker's data for two visually distinct rows. Trends are correct per-row, but the modal lookup is keyed only by ticker so the collision surfaces wrong per-row detail.
inTouched.why_it_matters: Yahoo tickers are not guaranteed unique across snapshot files (class-share suffixes, ADR vs local listing, refresh-universe churn). A silent overwrite means the dashboard shows row A's name/rank with row B's method results in the modal — a data-integrity defect that is invisible (no error, no log) and corrupts exactly the 'why did this rank here' explanation Karl relies on.
inTouched.fix: Detect ticker collisions when building rows: if `methodHistory[ticker]` or `stockDataMap[ticker]` is already populated for a different file, disambiguate the key (e.g. append the source filename) or skip-with-warn. Do NOT hardcode any ticker exclusion — make the de-dup key (ticker, file) or warn-and-keep-first. Add a comment naming the failure mode: 'prevents cross-listing ticker collision overwriting STOCK_DATA_MAP / modal detail'.

inTouched.title: Pass-count per method computed twice over the full M×N universe (renderHTML + main), result of first pass discarded
inTouched.evidence: renderHTML builds `_methodCounts` with a full sweep: line 516 `for (const r of rows) { for (const m of methods) { ... c.computable++ ... } }`. Then `main()` (line 1273) builds an IDENTICAL `passCounts` object with the same nested loop `for (const r of rows) { for (const m of methods) {...} }` purely to print the console summary. The `_methodCounts` computed in renderHTML is never returned, so main recomputes from scratch. At the projected 19k-ticker × ~83-method universe that is ~1.6M result-object accesses done twice (~3.2M).
inTouched.why_it_matters: This is exactly the 'wasted recompute over the universe' class the audit targets. The report-generator is on the 14.6h-projected critical path; a redundant full M×N sweep per run is pure waste and scales linearly with the universe growth the screener is trying to enable.
inTouched.fix: Compute the per-method counts once and reuse. Either have renderHTML return its `_methodCounts` (or accept a precomputed map), or compute the counts in `main()` before `renderHTML` and pass them in. Single source of truth for pass/computable counts. Add a comment naming the failure mode: 'prevents duplicate O(M×N) pass-count sweep on the 19k-ticker critical path'.

inTouched.title: Per-row `passList` rebuilt via Object.entries inside the nested Top-N-per-method card render (O(methods²) per card row)
inTouched.evidence: Inside `methods.filter(isCore).map(...)` (line 768) the inner `list.slice(0,TOP_N).map((r,i) => {...})` recomputes for EVERY rendered card row: line 821 `for (const [mid2, res2] of Object.entries(r.results)) { if (res2.computable && res2.pass === true) passList.push(mid2); }`. The same `r` (stock row) appears in the top-50 list of MANY methods, so its full `results` object (~83 entries) is re-walked once per (method-card × appearance). With ~40 CORE cards × 50 rows each, and the same popular stocks recurring across cards, this is tens of thousands of full results-object scans that produce an identical `data-passes` string each time.
inTouched.why_it_matters: Redundant recompute of an immutable per-stock value (the set of passing method-ids never changes for a given row). It bloats report-generation time and grows with both universe size and method count — the two axes the screener wants to scale.
inTouched.fix: Precompute each row's passing-method-id list once (e.g. `r._passList = ...` during evaluateAllStocks, alongside `passCount`/`failedMethods` which are already computed there at line 134-144) and reuse the cached string in the card render. Add a comment: 'prevents re-deriving the immutable per-row passing-method set once per method-card appearance'.

inTouched.title: Leaderboard prof-state badge dereferences `state[0]` without guarding that `state` is a non-empty string
inTouched.evidence: Line 612: `const profState = (() => { const ps = r.results['profitability-state']; return ps && ps.computable && ps.components ? ps.components.state[0] : '?'; })();`. The guard stops at `ps.components` — it then indexes `ps.components.state[0]`. If a computable profitability-state result has `components` but `state` is null/undefined/empty (the `'NA'` fallback used elsewhere in this very file at lines 438, 496, 827 acknowledges `components.state` can be absent), `state[0]` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0')` and aborts the whole report render.
inTouched.why_it_matters: Every other prof-state read in this file (lines 438, 496, 808-811, 827) defensively handles a missing `components.state`; this leaderboard path does not. A single stock with a computable-but-stateless profitability-state result would crash report generation for the entire universe — the report is a workflow artifact, so the run fails.
inTouched.fix: Guard the field: `const state = ps && ps.computable && ps.components && ps.components.state; const profState = state ? state[0] : '?';`. Mirror the existing `'NA'`/`'?'` fallback used elsewhere. Comment: 'prevents TypeError when profitability-state is computable but components.state is absent'.

inTouched.title: Matrix table ranks over ALL rows (incl. DataGuard-disqualified) while every other ranked surface ranks over discoveryRows — asymmetric attrition
inTouched.evidence: The deep-dive (line 310 `discoveryRows.filter`), the per-method Top-N cards (line 267-277 `discoveryRows`), and the Kennzahl-Rangliste (line 589 `discoveryRows.filter`) were all deliberately switched to rank over `discoveryRows` (DataGuard-disqualified excluded) per the 'F-A-2026-06-21' fixes. But the Matrix table still sorts and slices `[...rows]` (line 469) — the full set including disqualified stocks — then takes the top 300. A stock hard-failed by a DataGuard (e.g. sloan-ratio, revenue-shock-guard) can therefore appear in the Matrix top-300 but is intentionally absent from every other ranked surface and is counted in the header's 'disqualified by DataGuards' tally.
inTouched.why_it_matters: Inconsistent survivorship across surfaces: the header advertises N stocks as disqualified, yet the Matrix (the 'ranked exploration' surface) still surfaces them, while the leaderboards/cards/deep-dive hide them. This is the asymmetric-attrition data-integrity class — the same universe is filtered differently depending on which table you read, undermining trust in the screen.
inTouched.fix: Decide one policy. If disqualified stocks should be visible-but-flagged in the Matrix, mark them (e.g. a 'DQ' badge) rather than silently mixing them into the ranking; if they should be excluded like everywhere else, sort/slice `matrixRanked` from `discoveryRows`. Given the other four surfaces already use discoveryRows, ranking the Matrix over discoveryRows is the consistent fix. Comment: 'prevents asymmetric DataGuard attrition between Matrix and the leaderboards/deep-dive/header count'.

inTouched.title: Division by `rows.length` with no zero-guard — empty snapshots dir yields NaN%/Infinity in sector + header output
inTouched.evidence: Line 246: `const pct = (s.count / rows.length * 100);` and line 718 header: `${rows.length - discoveryRows.length} disqualified`. If `evaluateAllStocks` returns `[]` (empty/zeroed snapshots dir — a real failure mode after a botched pull, or when the `!f.startsWith('_')` filter on line 44 excludes everything), `rows.length === 0` makes every sector `pct` NaN and the file still writes 'successfully' (exit 0) with a NaN-riddled report. There is no 'no data' early-out.
inTouched.why_it_matters: Silent success on empty input is the swallowed-error / non-fail-loud class. A pull that produced zero usable snapshots should make the report-generator fail loudly (or emit an explicit 'no data' page), not write a green-looking HTML full of NaN that GitHub Pages then serves as if it were a valid screen.
inTouched.fix: Early-out in `main()` when `rows.length === 0`: log an error and `process.exit(1)` (or write an explicit empty-state page). Guard the `pct` math with `rows.length ? (s.count/rows.length*100) : 0`. Comment: 'prevents silent NaN report on an empty/failed snapshot set'.

inTouched.title: `||` fallback on ticker treats a falsy-but-valid `meta.ticker` as missing (latent falsy-coalescing bug)
inTouched.evidence: Line 90: `const ticker = (stock.meta && stock.meta.ticker) || file.replace(/\.json$/, '');`. This is the `|| fallback` falsy pattern the audit flags: an empty-string `meta.ticker` (a plausible bad-data shape from a malformed snapshot) is silently replaced by the filename stem rather than being caught as a data defect. The neighbouring lines were deliberately migrated from `||` to `?? null` / explicit `!= null` (lines 91-102, 168-169 comments cite F-GR-005) precisely to avoid this class, but the ticker line still uses `||`.
inTouched.why_it_matters: Inconsistent with the file's own hardening policy. While an empty ticker is rare, masking it behind the filename hides a corrupt snapshot instead of surfacing it, and a filename-derived ticker can diverge from the intended identity (feeding the collision risk in finding 01).
inTouched.fix: Use an explicit check: `const metaTicker = stock.meta && stock.meta.ticker; const ticker = (metaTicker != null && metaTicker !== '') ? metaTicker : file.replace(/\.json$/, '');` and consider warning when the meta ticker is empty. Comment: 'prevents empty-string meta.ticker being silently masked by the filename (matches F-GR-005 != null policy)'.

inTouched.title: methodHistory fallback to alert-state only fires when sidecar yields ZERO keys — a partially-populated sidecar permanently masks legacy history
inTouched.evidence: Lines 51-58 load `method-history-state.json` into `methodHistory`; lines 59-64 only read the legacy `alert-state.json` if `!Object.keys(methodHistory).length`. If the sidecar exists but is partial (e.g. a half-migrated or truncated sidecar with even one ticker's history), `Object.keys(methodHistory).length` is non-zero, so the legacy fallback is skipped entirely and every ticker absent from the partial sidecar permanently shows an empty trend column. Both JSON.parse failures are swallowed (`catch (e) { /* ignore */ }`).
inTouched.why_it_matters: Trend data silently degrades to 'n/a' for the majority of tickers whenever the sidecar is incomplete, with no warning — the swallowed-catch + all-or-nothing fallback hides a real migration/corruption problem. Trends are a primary signal in the matrix and modal.
inTouched.fix: Merge rather than all-or-nothing: load legacy alert-state history and the sidecar, with sidecar taking precedence per-ticker (`methodHistory = { ...legacy, ...sidecar }`). At minimum, log a warning on JSON.parse failure instead of silently ignoring (mirror the `_warnMediansLoad` loud-fallback pattern already used in methods/_helpers.js). Comment: 'prevents a partial sidecar from permanently masking legacy trend history'.

inTouched.title: Matrix column sort coerces mixed text via parseFloat-strip, mis-ordering values that share numeric prefixes (e.g. money suffixes)
inTouched.evidence: Line 1066: `var an = parseFloat(av.replace(/[^0-9.-]/g, ''));`. For the MCap column the cell text is formatted by `fmtMoney` as e.g. '$1.2T', '$900.0B', '$50M'. Stripping non-numerics yields 1.2, 900.0, 50 — so a $1.2T company sorts BELOW a $900B and a $50M company (1.2 < 50 < 900) because the magnitude suffix (T/B/M) is discarded. Same defect for any column whose display encodes magnitude in a suffix.
inTouched.why_it_matters: Client-side sort silently produces a wrong ranking for the MCap (and any suffix-scaled) column — the user sorts by market cap and gets nonsense order, eroding trust in the tool. It is a correctness bug in a primary interaction, not a cosmetic one.
inTouched.fix: Sort numeric columns off a `data-sort-value` attribute carrying the raw number (the matrix rows already have `r.marketCap` available at render time) rather than reverse-parsing the formatted text. For the generic handler, detect and apply the T/B/M/K multiplier when stripping. Comment: 'prevents magnitude-suffix loss making MCap sort order incorrect'.
